q: What is the core aim of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)?
options: Universal access to banking, with at least one basic bank account for every household
Cash subsidy to farmers for buying seeds
Encouraging households to invest in gold
Providing funds to join the mutual fund market
explain: PMJDY is the National Mission on Financial Inclusion: a basic account per household plus financial literacy, credit, insurance and pension access.

q: Which of the following is the tagline of the PMJDY?
explain: The tagline of Jan Dhan Yojana is Mera Khata Bhagya Vidhata; the other lines are look-alike distractors.

q: On which date did the Prime Minister announce PMJDY as the National Mission on Financial Inclusion in his Independence Day address?
explain: The announcement was made in the Independence Day speech of 15 August 2014. The three social security schemes followed on 9 May 2015.

q: Approximately how many PMJDY accounts were opened on the day of launch?
explain: About 1.5 crore accounts were opened on the launch day, a record for a single day.

q: Under PMJDY, which type of debit card is issued to every account holder?
explain: PMJDY account holders get a RuPay debit card, which carries an inbuilt accident insurance cover.

q: As per the scheme as described in the 2024-25 study material, the RuPay card of a PMJDY account carries an inbuilt accident insurance cover of
explain: The RuPay card of a PMJDY account carries an inbuilt accident cover of Rs 2 lakh (the cover was Rs 1 lakh for older accounts).

q: After how many months of satisfactory operation does a PMJDY account holder become eligible for an overdraft facility?
explain: Overdraft is available after six months of satisfactory operation of the account or credit history.

q: What is the revised overdraft limit under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana?
explain: To make PMJDY more attractive, the overdraft facility was doubled from Rs 5,000 to Rs 10,000.

q: Under PMJDY, each Sub Service Area (SSA) typically comprises how many households?
explain: Over 6 lakh villages were mapped into 1.59 lakh SSAs, each typically with 1,000 to 1,500 households.

q: In how many branchless Sub Service Areas were Bank Mitras deployed under PMJDY?
explain: 1.59 lakh is the total number of SSAs; 1.26 lakh of them had no bank branch and got Bank Mitras.

q: On 26 March 2020, the Finance Minister announced how much per month for three months to women Jan Dhan account holders during Covid-19?
explain: Rs 500 per month for the next three months was announced for every woman Jan Dhan account holder on 26 March 2020.

q: Which of the following schemes was NOT launched on 9 May 2015?
options: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
explain: PMJJBY, PMSBY and APY were launched together on 9 May 2015; PMMY (Mudra) was launched on 8 April 2015.

q: What is the age group for enrolling in the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY)?
explain: PMJJBY is for ages 18-50. 18-70 belongs to PMSBY and 18-40 to APY.

q: What is the maximum age limit for enrolling under the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?
explain: PMSBY covers people aged 18 to 70 who hold a bank account.

q: What was the annual premium of PMSBY at launch (as given in the study material)?
explain: PMSBY premium is Rs 12 a year; Rs 330 was the PMJJBY premium in the same material.

q: What is the coverage period of PMSBY and PMJJBY in a year?
explain: Cover runs from 1 June to 31 May and renews annually; auto-debit consent is due on or before 31 May.

q: What is the annual premium of the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana (PMJJBY) as given in the study material?
explain: PMJJBY gives Rs 2 lakh life cover for an annual premium of Rs 330 (as per the source; premiums were revised later).

q: Which of these schemes is offered by public sector general insurance companies through tie-ups with banks?
options: Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
explain: PMSBY is an accident cover sold by general insurers; PMJJBY and PMVVY are LIC products, and APY runs through banks and post offices.

q: Which of the following correctly describes the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana (PMSBY)?
options: A life insurance scheme for death due to any cause
An accidental death and disability insurance scheme
explain: PMSBY pays Rs 2 lakh on accidental death or full disability and Rs 1 lakh on partial disability.

q: What is the age group for joining the Atal Pension Yojana (APY)?
explain: APY is open to savings bank or post office savings account holders aged 18 to 40.

q: Under APY, the guaranteed monthly pension options are
options: Rs 1,000 to Rs 5,000 in steps of Rs 1,000
Rs 500 to Rs 2,500 in steps of Rs 500
Rs 2,000 to Rs 10,000 in steps of Rs 2,000
Rs 1,000 to Rs 10,000 in steps of Rs 1,000
explain: The pension options are Rs 1,000, 2,000, 3,000, 4,000 or 5,000 a month, payable from age 60.

q: Under APY, after the death of both the subscriber and the spouse, the accumulated pension corpus is returned to
options: The bank that holds the account
explain: Pension goes to the subscriber, then the spouse; the corpus built up to age 60 is returned to the nominee.

q: If APY contributions earn less than the estimated return, who funds the shortfall in the guaranteed pension?
explain: The minimum pension is guaranteed by the Government of India; if returns are higher, subscribers get enhanced benefits.

q: Which of the following is NOT listed among the APY service providers?
explain: APY runs through public and private sector banks, RRBs, cooperative banks and the Department of Posts.

q: On which date was the Atal Pension Yojana launched?
explain: APY was launched by the Prime Minister on 9 May 2015 along with PMJJBY and PMSBY.

q: When was the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana (PMMY) launched?
explain: Mudra was launched on 8 April 2015; Stand Up India followed on 5 April 2016.

q: Under the Mudra sub-scheme 'Kishore', loans are given in the range of
explain: Shishu is up to Rs 50,000, Kishore Rs 50,000-5 lakh and Tarun Rs 5-10 lakh.

q: Stand Up India scheme promotes entrepreneurship among which groups?
explain: Stand Up India helps SC/ST and women borrowers, who face hurdles of mentorship and credit, set up new ventures.

q: Stand Up India facilitates bank loans of what size per borrower?
explain: The loans are between Rs 10 lakh and Rs 1 crore for greenfield enterprises.

q: Which fund provides collateral-free coverage to loans under Stand Up India?
options: Credit Risk Guarantee Fund Trust for Micro and Small Enterprises
Credit Guarantee Fund for Stand Up India (CGFSI)
explain: CGFSI was set up by the Government to give collateral-free cover under Stand Up India.

q: The Pradhan Mantri Vaya Vandana Yojana (PMVVY) is meant for persons aged
explain: PMVVY protects elderly persons aged 60 and above against a fall in interest income.

q: What is the assured rate of return under PMVVY?
explain: PMVVY gives an assured 8% a year for 10 years, with pension monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly.

q: The maximum deposit limit under the Senior Citizens Savings Scheme (SCSS) was raised from Rs 15 lakh to Rs 30 lakh effective from
explain: The increase aligns with the Budget 2023 announcement and took effect on 1 April 2023.

q: On which date were the Gold Monetization Scheme, Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme and Indian Gold Coin launched?
explain: All three gold schemes were announced in Budget 2015-16 and launched by the Prime Minister on 5 November 2015.

q: What is the main aim of the Sovereign Gold Bond Scheme?
options: Collect gold jewellery from temples only
Provide a financial investment instrument and reduce the demand for physical gold
explain: SGBs reduce physical gold demand and, in the long run, gold imports.

q: The first tranche of Sovereign Gold Bonds was open for subscription during
explain: The first tranche ran from 6 November to 30 November 2015 and drew about Rs 250 crore.

q: Tax-free bonds of how much were allowed to be issued by CPSEs in Financial Year 2015-16?
explain: Government allowed Rs 40,000 crore of tax-free bonds in 2015-16, with tenures of 10, 15 or 20 years.

q: Which of the following is NOT named as an issuer of tax-free bonds in the study material?
explain: The named issuers are CPSEs such as NHAI, IRFC, HUDCO, IREDA, PFC, REC and NTPC; SBI is a bank.

q: On which date was Startup India launched?
explain: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016; its team reports to DPIIT.

q: How big a corpus fund does the 19-Point Startup India Action Plan envisage?
explain: The action plan includes incubation centres, easier patent filing, tax exemptions and a Rs 10,000 crore corpus fund.

q: The Sustainable Finance Scheme for funding green MSME projects was introduced by
explain: SIDBI introduced it for energy efficiency and cleaner production projects; NABARD runs JIVA.

q: NABARD launched the JIVA programme to promote
explain: JIVA is an agro-ecology programme under watershed and wadi programmes, launched on 9 February 2022.

q: How many ministries are brought together on the digital platform of PM Gati Shakti?
explain: The platform links 16 ministries including rail and roadways for integrated infrastructure planning.

q: The Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan was announced in May 2020 as a package of about
explain: The package was announced in four tranches by the Finance Minister.

q: The Ujala Yojana is implemented by which agency under the Ministry of Power?
explain: EESL, a joint venture of PSUs, implements Ujala to promote energy efficiency.

q: On which date was Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT) launched?
explain: DBT sends subsidies directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts, using Aadhaar linkage.

q: In the DBT system, funds move to Aadhaar-enabled accounts through which bridge?
explain: The Aadhaar Payment Bridge transfers funds on the basis of the Aadhaar number.

q: On which date was NREGA renamed the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme?
explain: NREGA was enacted in 2005 and renamed on Gandhi Jayanti, 2 October 2009.

q: How much income support does the PM-KISAN scheme provide to eligible farmer families per year?
explain: PM-KISAN pays Rs 6,000 a year in three 4-monthly instalments of Rs 2,000.

q: What amount was allocated to PM-KISAN in the Union Budget 2022-23?
explain: Rs 68,000 crore was allocated, against Rs 65,000 crore Budget Estimate of 2021-22.

q: Which statement about the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana is correct?
options: It treats the whole village as the unit of insurance
It treats the individual farmer as the unit of insurance and has the lowest-ever premium
Farmers pay a flat 10% premium on every crop
explain: PMFBY uses the individual farmer as the unit, with premiums of 2% (kharif), 1.5% (rabi) and 5% (commercial and horticultural).

q: Which facilities are provided to fishermen under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)?
options: Only a cash prize for the biggest catch
Insurance cover, financial assistance and Kisan Credit Card facility
explain: PMMSY, part of Atmanirbhar Bharat with Rs 20,050 crore, gives fishermen insurance, financial aid and KCC.

q: Mukhyamantri Ladli Behna Yojana was launched by which state government?
explain: The Madhya Pradesh scheme gives women Rs 1,000 a month.

q: Which state government launched the Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Yojana?
explain: It is on the lines of PM-Kisan; Maharashtra tops up Rs 6,000 to Rs 12,000 a year.

q: Which Union Ministry announced the creation of the 'Integrated Pensioners' Portal'?
explain: The Department of Pension and Pensioners' Welfare, under the Ministry of Personnel, will combine all pension portals.

q: Which Union Ministry launched the 'Vivad se Vishwas II (Contractual Disputes)' scheme?
explain: It is a settlement scheme for contractual disputes with government vendors, announced in the Union Budget.

q: The transaction limit for UPI payments for Retail Direct Scheme and IPO subscriptions was raised in December 2021 to
explain: The limit was increased to Rs 5 lakh in December 2021.

q: Which statement is true about the e-Rupee (digital rupee) of the RBI?
options: It is a private cryptocurrency not backed by RBI
It is interchangeable one-to-one with fiat currency and held in a digital wallet
It can only be used for gold purchases
It is not legal tender and trades at a variable price
explain: The retail e-Rupee pilot began on 1 December 2022; it is a sovereign currency at par with notes and coins.

q: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP) has a minimum investment of Rs 1,000. What is the maximum investment limit?
explain: KVP has no upper limit on investment and a lock-in of 30 months.

q: Which tool did the Economic Survey 2016-17 recommend as an alternative to subsidy-focused welfare schemes?
explain: The Survey recommended exploring a Universal Basic Income instead of many subsidy-based schemes.
